name: How early should retail fixtures be selected during design?

mainEntity.name: How early should retail fixtures, shelving, and display systems be selected in the design process?
mainEntity.text: How early should retail fixtures, shelving, and display systems be selected in the design process?

acceptedAnswer.text: Retail fixtures, shelving, and display systems should be selected early because they affect nearly every part of the build-out. Fixture dimensions can change aisle widths, checkout placement, lighting locations, power needs, and even code clearances. If the owner waits until late in the process, the contractor may need to revise drawings or adjust rough-in work, which increases cost and delays the schedule. Early selection also helps with procurement, since some fixtures are custom or have long lead times. The best approach is to confirm the merchandising concept while the plans are still flexible. That way, the store is built around the actual product display strategy instead of forcing the fixtures into a finished space.
acceptedAnswer.description: Retail fixtures should be selected early, ideally during schematic design, because they affect layout, electrical placement, lighting, millwork, and lead times. Waiting too long can create redesigns and delay installation.
